items.title: Linearly realized Standard Model EFT field and scale data
items.design_state: Adopts the linearly realized three-family Standard Model field and gauge data and a finite B- and L-conserving canonical-dimension-six local model, with explicit scales and physical limits.
items.statement: Adopt four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^0=ct$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ for engineering dimensions, so $\partial_\mu$ has mass dimension one, a scalar field has dimension one, a spinor field has dimension $3/2$, and a gauge field strength has dimension two.

references.title: B. Grzadkowski, M. Iskrzynski, M. Misiak and J. Rosiek, Dimension-Six Terms in the Standard Model Lagrangian
references.locator: §§1–3, printed pp. 1–5: the SM gauge group, field representations, natural field dimensions, canonical-dimension expansion and dimension-six coefficient convention.

references.title: Adam Falkowski, Lectures on SMEFT
references.locator: §2 and Table 1, printed pp. 5–8: assumptions behind SMEFT and the SM field representations; §§3.1–3.4, printed pp. 7–14: canonical-dimension power counting and dimension-six operators.

items.title: Nonlinear electroweak Goldstone and scalar-singlet EFT data
items.design_state: Adopts the nonlinear SU(2)-valued Goldstone field and independent scalar singlet with the exact right hypercharge action and separate HEFT scales.
items.statement: Use the same four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, direct-product global gauge group, gauge connection, fermion representations, family content, and the preceding model's exact baryon- and lepton-number selection rules on formal local interactions. No anomaly-free quantum-current claim is made. In particular, the hypercharge-one-half Higgs doublet of that model is replaced in this realization by three angular Goldstone coordinates and a real scalar singlet; this is a distinct adopted model interface, not a deduction that the two models have identical field spaces.

references.title: Gerhard Buchalla, Oscar Catà and Claudius Krause, Complete Electroweak Chiral Lagrangian with a Light Higgs at NLO
references.locator: §2, printed pp. 2–3, equations (1)–(9): nonlinear Goldstone matrix, singlet h, transformation law and leading scalar Lagrangian; Appendix A, printed pp. 22–23, arbitrary functions of h/v.

references.title: Rodrigo Alonso, A Primer on Higgs Effective Field Theory with Geometry
references.locator: §3.2, printed pp. 14–15, HEFT building blocks and U/h transformation roles; §4, printed pp. 15–17, the HEFT expansion and separate scale.

items.title: Finite dimension-six Warsaw coefficient contract
items.design_state: Defines the source-listed B- and L-conserving dimension-six Warsaw coefficient representatives and their family and conjugation conventions without claiming a local classification proof.
items.statement: Use the fields, direct-product gauge group, hypercharge normalization, three-family content, exact $U(1)_B\times U(1)_L$ symmetries, natural units and coefficient scale of the preceding linearly realized model. A local operator is a finite polynomial in these fields and their covariant derivatives at one spacetime point, with all Lorentz, gauge and family indices contracted to a Lorentz and gauge scalar. Its canonical dimension assigns one to $H$ and each derivative, $3/2$ to a fermion, and two to a field strength.

references.title: B. Grzadkowski, M. Iskrzynski, M. Misiak and J. Rosiek, Dimension-Six Terms in the Standard Model Lagrangian
references.locator: §2 and Table 1, printed pp. 2–3, for field, hypercharge, index and sign conventions; §§3 and 5–7, printed pp. 4–14, for the B-conserving operator representatives and their stated EOM, integration-by-parts and Fierz reductions.

references.title: Adam Falkowski, Lectures on SMEFT
references.locator: Table 1 and §§3.4–4, printed pp. 8–20, for the three-family dimension-six Warsaw coefficient convention, basis nonuniqueness and field-redefinition/EOM caveat.

items.title: Finite electroweak HEFT chiral and loop counting
items.design_state: Defines the source-convention HEFT chiral and loop grading and finite NLO classes separately from canonical-dimension counting.
items.statement: Use the HEFT fields $U$, $h$, gauge curvatures, fermions and arbitrary smooth coefficient functions of $h/v$ from the preceding HEFT model. The canonical engineering dimension $\Delta$ is the mass weight of the local polynomial in fields and derivatives; it is the weight supplied by the finite-jet operator definition. The **chiral/loop count** is separate data and is not inferred from $\Delta$.

references.title: Gerhard Buchalla, Oscar Catà and Claudius Krause, Complete Electroweak Chiral Lagrangian with a Light Higgs at NLO
references.locator: §3, printed pp. 3–4, equations (10)–(12), for the diagram degree and the finite one-loop counterterm classes; §§4.1–4.6, printed pp. 4–11, for the operator structures.

references.title: Rodrigo Alonso, A Primer on Higgs Effective Field Theory with Geometry
references.locator: §§3.2–4, printed pp. 14–17, on the h/v functions, Goldstone building blocks and the distinction between canonical-dimension and HEFT expansions.

references.title: Adam Falkowski, Lectures on SMEFT
references.locator: §3.1, printed pp. 7–8, on canonical-dimension power counting for SMEFT, used here only to state the separate counting.

items.design_state: Proves the smooth equivariant nonzero-doublet patch map and the finite polynomial and coefficient-image restrictions of the selected SMEFT branch.
